instruction: DWG/DXF Floor-Plan Import with Cleanup The file `C:\Users\user\Desktop\messy.dxf` is a 2D floor plan of a small single-storey house (real-world footprint ~7.6 m x 5.0 m with one interior partition). The file was authored in a CAD program whose user typed dimensions in millimetres, but the DXF header was left declaring its insert-units as Inches (`$INSUNITS = 1`). A downstream consumer reading the file at face value therefore sees a ~193 m x 127 m building - 25.4 x too large. On top of that, two cleanliness problems make the file inconvenient to import: 1. Wall polylines are scattered across three layer names: `WALL-EXT`, `wall_ext`, and the canonical `WALL`. All three really mean the same thing. 2. Three wall polylines have been drawn twice (same endpoints, different wall-layer variants) - classic copy-paste / CAD round-trip artefacts. Non-wall layers (`DIMS`, `GRID`) are also present and must pass through unchanged. Your task is to implement a robust cleanup pass and write TWO output files: # C:\Users\user\Desktop\cleaned.dxf A re-emitted DXF in which: - **Units mismatch fixed.** Detect that the geometry, when interpreted per the file's declared unit, exceeds a building-plausible maximum dimension (> 30 m). Apply a correction factor of `1 / 25.4` and re-emit with `$INSUNITS = Meters`. Concretely, the cleaned polylines' coordinates must lie in a building-plausible range `5 m <= max_dim <= 30 m` (here: 7.6 m x 5.0 m). - **Wall layers consolidated.** Every polyline on `WALL-EXT` or `wall_ext` is reassigned to the canonical layer `WALL`. No polyline on a wall-alias layer survives in the cleaned output. - **Duplicate wall polylines removed.** Two polylines on WALL-ish layers with the same endpoint set (order-independent, 1 mm tolerance) are considered duplicates; only one copy survives. - Stray layers (`DIMS`, `GRID`) and their entities pass through unchanged (after scaling). # C:\Users\user\Desktop\report.json A JSON object describing the transforms you applied, matching this exact schema: ```json { "scale_factor": 0.03937007874015748, "layer_consolidations": {"WALL-EXT": "WALL", "wall_ext": "WALL"}, "duplicate_polylines_removed": 3 } ``` - `scale_factor` is the detected correction multiplier (here, `1 / 25.4 approx 0.03937`) - NOT the net mm-to-m scale. - `layer_consolidations` maps every alias that you rewrote to its canonical target. Both `WALL-EXT` and `wall_ext` must map to `WALL`. - `duplicate_polylines_removed` is an integer count (> 0) of the wall polylines you dropped as duplicates, and must equal `<wall polylines in input> - <wall polylines in cleaned output>`. Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\cleaned.dxf` parses via ezdxf. 2. All wall LWPOLYLINE/POLYLINE entities in the cleaned output are on layer `WALL` (no `WALL-EXT` or `wall_ext` leaks). 3. At least 4 wall polylines survive (the 5 unique walls, minus any that your dedup logic conservatively removes). 4. No duplicate wall polylines (same endpoint set within 1 mm) remain. 5. Max XY dimension of cleaned geometry lies in `[5, 30]` m. 6. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\report.json` parses and is a JSON object. 7. `report.scale_factor` is numeric and within 5 % of `1 / 25.4`. 8. `report.layer_consolidations` is an object with `WALL-EXT -> WALL` AND `wall_ext -> WALL`. 9. `report.duplicate_polylines_removed` is a positive integer and equals the actual number of polylines dropped (input wall polylines minus cleaned wall polylines). [Software] Launch SketchUp with `C:\SketchUp 2026 26.0.429 x64 En Portable\SketchUp.exe` (adjust if your install differs).
